notes.decision: Running book-title header 'of the Teacher' (ⲙⲡⲥⲁⲍ = ⲙⲡⲥⲁϩ). Standard alternating header in the codex (recto/verso pair: 'The Kephalaia' / 'of the Teacher'). Not a new chapter heading.
Restored '[stand fast]' from ⲧⲱⲕ ⲉⲣⲁⲧ⸗ idiom 'stand firm/stand up.' ⲟⲩⲃⲏⲓ̈ = 'before me / opposite me.' Editor's restoration accepted.

ⲁⲓ̈ⲗⲟ = 'I ceased' (ⲗⲟ 'cease' + ⲉⲓ̈- circumstantial). The verb governed by ⲉⲓ̈ⲃⲛ is unclear — ⲃⲛ does not yield a recognizable Lycopolitan root and may be a scribal corruption (possibly for ⲍⲛ̄ 'in,' giving 'while I was in light,' or for some lost verb of perception/expression). Translated cautiously as 'I ceased my [...] of the light.' The parallel construction in L2 ('I ceased speaking with frankness') suggests a verb of communication or display.
ⲡⲁⲣⲍⲏⲥⲓⲁ = Greek παρρησία 'frankness, bold speech' (with Lycopolitan ⲍ for ϩ/ρ-cluster). ⲡⲍⲣⲁⲩ = ⲡϩⲣⲟⲟⲩ 'the voice.' 'I ceased speaking with frankness in the voice that is of [tr]uth.'
Read as ⲉⲧⲃⲉ + ⲁⲓⲧ ⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ 'concerning that which has come / been done to me' — ⲁⲓⲧ as qualitative or perfect of ⲉⲓ 'come' / ⲉⲓⲣⲉ 'do.' The ⲁⲓⲧ ⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ idiom suggests something befalling Mani.
ϫⲛⲉⲩ = 'they asked' or interrogative 'are there?' Following the vacat (paragraph break), this opens a new section, possibly with a question put to Mani.
ⲡⲍⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩ = ⲡϩⲏⲧ-ⲟⲩ 'their midst/inwardness' or ⲡϩⲱⲛ-ⲧⲟⲩ 'their assembly.' ϩⲁⲣ̄ ⲟⲩⲏⲓ̈ literally 'under one (house)' = 'together / under one roof.' Rendered 'in their midst together.'

Greek-Coptic hybrid: συμπ- (or ϩⲩⲡⲟ-) prefix + ⲁⲉϫⲉ (Lycopolitan ϣⲁϫⲉ 'speak'). The compound functions like συμβουλεύω/συνλαλέω = 'deliberate, confer, discuss together.' Translated 'I conferred / deliberated.' Same form recurs L11.
ⲙⲉⲓⲍⲟⲛ = Greek μείζονες 'great ones, magnates.' ⲥⲩⲣⲕⲗⲏⲧⲓⲕⲟⲥ = Greek συγκλητικοί 'councillors, senators.' Court-officer titles in the Sasanian context.
Greek σατράπαι 'satraps' and ἡγεμόνες 'governors.' Sasanian provincial administrators.

ⲍⲣⲁⲱ = ⲁⲣⲉϩ 'guard, keep' (Lycopolitan ⲍ-prosthetic). ⲁⲣⲉϩ ⲁⲣⲟ⸗ ⲙ̄- = 'guard oneself against.' ⲡⲉϩⲕⲓⲙ likely = ⲡ-ⲁⲧ-ⲕⲓⲙ 'the unmoved/unmoving' (Lycopolitan ⲁⲧ-→ⲉϩ-) or ⲡⲉⲧ-ⲕⲓⲙ 'that which moves.' Reading as 'the unmoved' fits the spiritual context of guarding firmness; alternative 'against being moved/shaken' also possible. Translated 'I have kept guard over the unmoved.'

ⲟⲩⲉ̄ⲍⲏ likely ⲟⲩⲉϩⲏ 'a way / front / first thing.' ⲉⲡⲉⲓⲁⲏ = ἐπειδή 'since/because.' ⲉⲩⲏⲡ = qualitative of ⲱⲡ 'count/reckon' = 'they are counted.' ⲁⲣⲁϩ here = 'with/to.' Rendered '[...]a way, since they are reckoned with [...].'
ⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ⲛⲟⲃⲉ 'sinners' (lit. 'doers of sin') with Lycopolitan ⲣⲉϩ- for ⲣⲉϥ-. 'all the sinners.'
ⲍⲣⲁⲙ probably scribal variant of ⲍⲣⲁⲱ (= ⲁⲣⲉϩ 'guard'); same construction as L7. ⲡⲁⲣⲁ ⲛⲉⲓ̈ = 'beyond/more than these.' 'I have guarded myself beyond all these.'
ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ = 'draw inward, pull in.' Circumstantial: 'while drawing me inward to [...].' ⲛ̄- here marks the circumstantial conjunction.
ⲙⲉⲓ̈ⲉ = ⲙⲉ 'to love.' ⲕⲉⲕⲉ = ⲕⲁⲕⲉ 'darkness.' 'The world loves the darkness.' Standard Manichaean dualistic formula.

ⲙⲟⲥⲧⲉ = 'to hate.' ⲍⲱⲙϩ I read as Lycopolitan variant of ⲱⲙⲥ 'submerge, drown, extinguish' (ϩ for ⲥ in some Lycopolitan positions). Pair: 'hates [and ext]inguishes the light' — perfect cosmic formula complementing 'loves the darkness.' Editor's restoration of ⲉϩⲙⲁⲥⲧⲉ accepted.
ϩⲃⲏⲩⲉ 'deeds' + restored ⲍⲁⲩ 'evil' — 'because the deeds [are evil].' Restoration is contextually plausible from the dualistic formula.
ⲝⲟⲟⲣⲉ = ϫⲓⲟⲟⲣⲉ/ⲭⲓⲟⲣⲉ 'cross over' (cf. accumulated vocabulary). 'I crossed the seas.' ⲛ̄ⲕⲉⲥⲁⲡ = 'another time / again.'
'I went up to the land of Persia.' ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ = 'upward/up to.' Restoration ⲡⲉⲣⲥⲓⲥ confirmed by L17 and L22.

ⲃⲁⲃⲧ — likely a verb of maritime travel; possibly ⲡⲱⲃⲧ 'cross over, plunge' or a form connected to ⲡⲱⲧ 'run.' Editor's restoration [ⲁⲓ̈ⲃ]ⲁⲃⲧ accepted; rendered '[I crossed]' provisionally. The clause clearly continues the maritime journey: 'up upon the sea.'
'In the living truth which is [with me / before me].' ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ = ⲉⲧⲟⲛϩ qualitative 'living.' ⲉⲧⲍⲁ[ⲧⲏⲓ̈] = ⲉⲧϩⲁⲧⲏⲓ̈ 'which is by me / with me.' † is the supralinear marker for sacred terms.
ⲧⲁϣⲉⲟⲉⲓϣ 'to proclaim, preach.' Standard Manichaean missionary verb. 'I have proclaimed [...] to the rulers (ἀρχαί) and the powers (ἐξουσίαι).'
Greek ἐξουσιασταί 'officials, men of authority.' Distinct from ⲉⲝⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ in L19 (the abstract 'powers'); these are concrete office-holders.
Greek φωστήρ 'luminary.' In Manichaean cosmology, the Luminaries are the Sun and Moon (the two ships) or by extension great Light-beings. Context fragmentary.
'body [...] concerning the truth that I have proclaimed.' ⲉⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲧⲁⲱⲉⲁⲓ̈ⲱ is relative perfect of ⲧⲁϣⲉⲟⲉⲓϣ.
'in their midst [...] to one another.' ⲁⲛⲉⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ = ⲁⲛⲉⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ 'to each other.'
ⲡⲟⲩⲕⲁⲍ = 'your (pl.) land.' ⲛⲧⲃⲁⲙ = 'the power of' (ϭⲟⲙ in Sahidic; Lycopolitan ⲧⲃⲁⲙ/ϭⲃⲁⲙ). 'in your land [...] to me the power of the Father.'
ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲛⲍ = ⲉⲧⲟⲛϩ 'living/that lives.' ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲱ = ⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓϣ 'time' — 'for all time / forever.'

proposed_terms.rationale: Greek-Coptic hybrid compound: συμπ- (or ϩⲩⲡⲟ-) prefix + ⲁⲉϫⲉ (Lycopolitan ϣⲁϫⲉ 'speak'). Functions like Greek συλλαλέω/συμβουλεύομαι 'speak together with, confer.' Used here twice (L5, L11) of Mani's discourses with court magnates. Distinct from simple ⲁⲉϫⲉ 'speak' or ⲧⲁϣⲉⲟⲉⲓϣ 'proclaim.'

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡ-ⲁⲧ-ⲕⲓⲙ 'the not-moving / unmovable,' with ⲁⲧ- privative prefix becoming ⲉϩ-. Alternative: relative ⲡⲉⲧ-ⲕⲓⲙ 'that which moves' (with ⲁⲣⲉϩ ⲁⲣⲁϩ ⲙ̄- = 'guard against'). The 'unmoved' reading fits the spiritual ideal of steadfastness Mani is claiming for himself in this autobiographical passage.

Lycopolitan variant of ⲱⲙⲥ 'submerge, drown, extinguish' (ϩ for final ⲥ). Paired with ⲙⲟⲥⲧⲉ 'hate' as the Cosmos's twin actions toward Light: 'hates and extinguishes the light' — complementing the parallel 'loves the darkness.' Cosmic-dualistic formula.

Lycopolitan ⲡϩⲏⲧ-ⲟⲩ '(in) their heart / midst' or ⲡϩⲱⲛ-ⲧⲟⲩ 'their assembly.' Used L4 'in their midst together (under one roof)' and L15 'of their midst.' Spatial/relational sense of being among or within.
Greek loanword μείζονες 'greater ones, magnates.' Sasanian court-officer category. Forms a hierarchy with ⲥⲩⲣⲕⲗⲏⲧⲓⲕⲟⲥ (councillors/senators), ⲥⲁⲧⲣⲁⲡⲧⲏⲥ (satraps), and ⲍⲏⲅⲉⲙⲱⲛ (governors).
